tooltip_texts.label: About Net sales
tooltip_texts.text: Product sales after returns in the last 12 months, for customers we can identify. This is revenue, not profit.

tooltip_texts.label: About Customers
tooltip_texts.text: Customers who bought in the last 12 months. The note below shows all retained accounts, including those who have not bought recently.

tooltip_texts.label: About Returns
tooltip_texts.text: The share of invoices that record a return in the last 12 months. A return may cover only part of an order.

tooltip_texts.label: About Expected profit from the campaign
tooltip_texts.text: Extra profit we expect from the proposed campaign after its costs. It depends on our assumptions about offer responses and margin.

tooltip_texts.label: About Sales at a glance
tooltip_texts.text: Countries follow the source Country field. Product sales and returns use the same country filter; overlapping source entries are counted once.

tooltip_texts.label: About How sales have changed
tooltip_texts.text: Chart shows complete months through Nov 2011; the headline uses the last 12 months. Dec 1–9: £339,118.97. £37,679.89 per calendar day, compared with £22,017.53 per day. The previous average covers Dec 2009–Nov 2011 (730 calendar days). December covers 9 days. Charts end at November; no full December month is estimated.

tooltip_texts.label: About Customer loyalty ranking
tooltip_texts.text: Loyalty combines how recently, how often and how much customers bought in the rolling year; score ties use customer ID. These 12 calendar columns are Jan–Dec 2011, with Dec (1-9) partial. Ranking spend also includes 10–31 Dec 2010.

tooltip_texts.label: About Who is likely to buy?
tooltip_texts.text: A purchase is one customer-day; counts and customer age use the full retained history. Age starts at the first observed purchase. Expected spend allows repeat purchases and is not profit or the extra sales caused by an offer.

tooltip_texts.label: About Customer
tooltip_texts.text: The customer’s identifier in the source data.

tooltip_texts.label: About Days since last purchase
tooltip_texts.text: Days from the customer’s last recorded purchase to 9 December 2011.

tooltip_texts.label: About Purchases
tooltip_texts.text: The number of days on which this customer bought something in the retained history. Several orders on one day count as one purchase.

tooltip_texts.label: About Time as customer (days)
tooltip_texts.text: Days from the customer’s first recorded purchase to 9 December 2011. This is the length of their recorded history, not their personal age.

tooltip_texts.label: About Probability of buying · 90 days
tooltip_texts.text: The estimated chance that the customer buys at least once in the next 90 days, even if we do nothing. It is not a guarantee.

tooltip_texts.label: About Expected spend · 90 days
tooltip_texts.text: What we expect the customer to spend in the next 90 days even if we do nothing.

tooltip_texts.label: About Returns
tooltip_texts.text: A return invoice can contain a partial return; it does not establish that the whole original order was cancelled. Values are revenue returned, not lost profit. Charts show complete months through Nov 2011; notes report the partial December period separately.

tooltip_texts.label: About Return invoices
tooltip_texts.text: Dec 1–9: 136.00. 15.11 per calendar day, compared with 9.79 per day. The previous average covers Dec 2009–Nov 2011 (730 calendar days). December covers 9 days. Charts end at November; no full December month is estimated.

tooltip_texts.label: About Value returned
tooltip_texts.text: Dec 1–9: £174,111.46. £19,345.72 per calendar day, compared with £738.22 per day. The previous average covers Dec 2009–Nov 2011 (730 calendar days). December covers 9 days. Charts end at November; no full December month is estimated.

tooltip_texts.label: About Share of invoices
tooltip_texts.text: Dec 1–9: 14.91%. Return invoices: 15.11 per day; previous average 9.79 per day. The previous average covers Dec 2009–Nov 2011 (730 calendar days). December covers 9 days. Charts end at November; no full December month is estimated.

tooltip_texts.label: About Reset proposal
tooltip_texts.text: Restore the starting budget, coupon limit and assumptions for the proposal.

tooltip_texts.label: About Budget (£)
tooltip_texts.text: The most we are willing to spend on emails and coupons.

tooltip_texts.label: About Maximum coupons
tooltip_texts.text: A ceiling on coupons, not a target.

tooltip_texts.label: About Advanced assumptions
tooltip_texts.text: Change the assumed margin, offer responses, costs and coupon discount used in the proposal.

tooltip_texts.label: About Margin (assumption, %)
tooltip_texts.text: The share of each pound of sales left after product costs, before campaign costs. This is an assumption, not measured from these data.

tooltip_texts.label: About Response to email (assumption, %)
tooltip_texts.text: The assumed share of customers who would not otherwise buy but buy because of an email. An A/B test would help estimate this.

tooltip_texts.label: About Response to coupon (assumption, %)
tooltip_texts.text: The assumed share of customers who would not otherwise buy but buy because of a coupon. An A/B test would help estimate this.

tooltip_texts.label: About Email cost (£)
tooltip_texts.text: The cost of sending one email, whether or not the customer buys.

tooltip_texts.label: About Coupon fixed cost (£)
tooltip_texts.text: The fixed cost of offering one coupon, before any discount on a purchase.

tooltip_texts.label: About Coupon discount (%)
tooltip_texts.text: The share taken off the purchase price when a customer uses the coupon.

tooltip_texts.label: About Proposed outreach
tooltip_texts.text: These are customers to contact, not confirmed reactivations. Expected profit values one purchase occasion; it is not total future customer spend.

tooltip_texts.label: About No contact
tooltip_texts.text: Customers we propose leaving without an email or coupon. No messages are sent from this demo.

tooltip_texts.label: About Email
tooltip_texts.text: Customers we propose sending an email to. This is a proposed action, not a confirmed purchase.

tooltip_texts.label: About Coupon
tooltip_texts.text: Customers we propose offering a coupon to. This is a proposed action, not a confirmed purchase.

tooltip_texts.label: About Total expected cost
tooltip_texts.text: What we expect to spend on emails, coupon costs and discounts for this proposal. It can be less than the budget.

tooltip_texts.label: About Expected profit
tooltip_texts.text: Extra profit we expect from the proposed campaign after its costs. It depends on our assumptions about offer responses and margin.

tooltip_texts.label: About Return on investment (ROI)
tooltip_texts.text: Expected extra profit divided by expected campaign cost. For example, £5.43 means £5.43 profit for each £1 spent. It depends on our assumptions.

tooltip_texts.label: About Customer
tooltip_texts.text: The customer’s identifier in the source data.

tooltip_texts.label: About Recommended action
tooltip_texts.text: The action proposed for this customer under the current budget, coupon limit and assumptions.

tooltip_texts.label: About Days since last purchase
tooltip_texts.text: Days from the customer’s last recorded purchase to 9 December 2011.

tooltip_texts.label: About Expected spend · 90 days
tooltip_texts.text: What we expect the customer to spend in the next 90 days even if we do nothing.

tooltip_texts.label: About Typical order value
tooltip_texts.text: The size of a typical purchase for this customer. Expected gain is the extra chance of buying created by the offer times this value times the margin, minus the cost.

tooltip_texts.label: About Expected gain
tooltip_texts.text: Extra profit we expect from this action after its cost; it depends on our assumption of how customers respond to the offer.

tooltip_texts.label: About Method and evidence
tooltip_texts.text: Select a model to inspect calibration. Lift ranks propensity; revenue capture ranks probability × expected order value.

tooltip_texts.label: About Calculation status
tooltip_texts.text: Status: FEASIBLE_GAP_TARGET. Native status: NOT_RUN_CERTIFIED_GAP. Actual gap: 0.0033%. Target: 0.5%. The bound applies to the plan using values rounded to pennies.

tooltip_texts.label: About Historical model comparison
tooltip_texts.text: The proposed campaign uses PROD's 09 Dec 2011 cutoff. The customer-account table always uses stored PROD/BG-NBD forecasts. Solver status and the actual certified gap are reported here, never presented as an estimated business effect. Run A underpredicts peak-season purchasing. PROD trains on that peak and scores an off-peak horizon; ML probabilities are expected to be overestimated, but future calibration is unverified. Loyalty uses R+F+M quintiles with average percentile ranks and ID tie-breaking; no-purchase-in-window accounts score 1+1+1. Heatmap colours use a logarithmic scale to preserve contrast across spend sizes. Forecasts, selection optimism, seasonality and campaign response assumptions are distinct limitations.

tooltip_texts.label: About Calibration
tooltip_texts.text: Dashed line: perfect calibration; points above it indicate underprediction.

tooltip_texts.label: About Baseline challenge
tooltip_texts.text: The improvement shown here compares the current interactive proposal with ratio greedy under the same assumptions. It uses unrounded expected profit, before formatting to pounds and pennies. A large improvement over the naive baseline does not establish a large gain over a sensible alternative.

tooltip_texts.label: About Sensitivity to budget and response
tooltip_texts.text: At most 15 scenarios, 0.5% gap target, no extra-budget solve. Other current campaign assumptions are held fixed. The default grid is precomputed at API startup.

tooltip_texts.label: About Run A: what was at stake, not campaign effect
tooltip_texts.text: These purchases occurred without the proposed campaign. Groups are selected, not randomized; the denominator excludes new customers acquired after cutoff. Buyer order value averages each buyer's spend / purchase occasions. Optimizing for high predicted value can select customers with overestimated order values; whole-group predictions and buyer-only outcomes have different populations (hover the prediction for the same-buyer mean). The model assumes the same action-response parameter tau for dormant customers (pi close to 0) as for other customers.

tooltip_texts.label: About Contacted-customer realized spend
tooltip_texts.text: What these customers actually spent in the historical period, before any campaign. It is a reference point, not a result.

tooltip_texts.label: About Share of eligible spend
tooltip_texts.text: The share of all eligible customers’ actual spending covered by the selected customers in the historical check. It does not show extra sales caused by a campaign.
